+# ADR 0001: Increase Pricing Cache TTL from 900 to 3600 Seconds
+
+**Status:** Accepted
+
+**Date:** 2026-07-24
+
+## Context
+
+The pricing service currently caches pricing data with a Time-To-Live (TTL) of 900 seconds (15 minutes). This relatively short TTL was established as a conservative default to balance responsiveness to pricing changes with cache effectiveness. However, analysis of pricing update patterns across our systems reveals that pricing data changes infrequently and unpredictably—most price updates occur during scheduled maintenance windows or planned promotions, not continuously throughout the day.
+
+The 15-minute cache window creates unnecessary load on the pricing service backend and increases latency for clients that miss the cache during high-traffic periods. Additionally, the frequency of cache invalidation causes cold starts that don't provide meaningful business value, as most requests occur for stable pricing within any given hour-long window.
+
+## Decision
+
+We will increase the pricing cache TTL from 900 seconds to 3600 seconds (1 hour). This longer cache window reduces backend load while maintaining reasonable freshness for pricing data. The decision acknowledges that pricing changes are infrequent enough that a one-hour cache window is acceptable for most use cases.
+
+For scenarios requiring real-time pricing accuracy (e.g., checkout flows during promotional windows), the application layer can implement explicit cache invalidation through existing invalidation endpoints, allowing critical paths to override the standard TTL when necessary.
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive:**
+- Reduced load on the pricing service backend by approximately 75%, as cache hit rates are expected to improve significantly with the longer TTL.
+- Lower latency for most clients, as more requests will be served from cache rather than requiring backend calls.
+- Reduced operational costs associated with pricing service infrastructure.
+
+**Negative:**
+- Pricing data may be stale by up to one hour. Clients querying pricing during the final minutes of a cache window will not immediately see recently updated prices.
+- External teams must be aware of the longer cache duration when coordinating time-sensitive pricing changes; they should use the explicit invalidation mechanism for critical updates.
+- Potential for user confusion during promotional transitions if cache invalidation is not coordinated properly.
+
+**Mitigations:**
+- Document the cache behavior in the pricing API specification, including the invalidation endpoint usage.
+- Establish alerting on the pricing service to detect when invalidation endpoints are not being used during coordinated pricing changes.
+- Provide client libraries with helper functions to request cache bypass when needed, using cache-control headers.
